Concise Clinical Note

Consult Summary:
• 26-year-old woman with 3-day gradually worsening right-eye–predominant headache with photophobia and visual “shooting lights”; clinical impression most consistent with a first episode of migraine.

History:
• Presenting complaint: Persistent headache ×3 days, worsening; started at work.  
• Character: Constant dull ache with intermittent sharper spikes; severity 8/10; global but maximal around right eye.  
• Associated symptoms: Photophobia (light hurts), transient visual scintillations at onset, nausea (“feel sick”), difficulty concentrating.  
• Pertinent negatives: No vomiting, no fever, no neck stiffness, no focal weakness, no speech disturbance, no rash, no head trauma.  
• Prior episodes: Occasional milder headaches responsive to ibuprofen; no prior diagnosed migraines.  
• Medications tried: Ibuprofen 3 tablets/day for 2 days without relief.  
• Past medical history: None reported.  
• Allergies: No known drug allergies.  
• Regular medications: None; not on oral contraceptive pill.  
• Family history: Mother and sister with recurrent migraines (mother severe, sister infrequent).  
• Social / preventive: IT professional (prolonged screen use), lives with three housemates; social smoker and drinker; mild job stress; wears glasses (no recent eye test).

Examination:
• Tele-visit; no vitals provided.  
• No focal neurological deficits reported by patient.  
• No overt signs of systemic illness described.

Impression:
• Likely migraine (possibly first onset, ± aura) – supported by unilateral/right-eye focus, photophobia, visual aura-like phenomena, nausea, female in 20s, strong family history, moderate–severe intensity, functional impairment.  
• Alternative considerations (less likely):  
  – Tension-type headache: diffuse dull pain with stress/computer use but photophobia and visual phenomena less typical.  
  – Acute sinusitis: right peri-orbital pain but lacks congestion, fever, facial tenderness.

Plan:
• Optimize NSAID dosing: educate patient that ibuprofen may be taken 400 mg (2 x 200 mg tablets) up to three times daily with food if no contraindications.  
• Offer prescription for stronger analgesia: Naproxen and/or addition of paracetamol ± short-course codeine if needed.  
• Headache diary: record timing, severity, potential triggers.  
• Preventive discussion deferred; reassess frequency at follow-up.  
• Eye care: advised to arrange routine eye test given prolonged screen use and photophobia.  
• Red-flag advice: return sooner or call if worsening headache, new visual loss, limb weakness, speech difficulty, vomiting, or systemic illness.  
• Follow-up: clinic review in 1–2 weeks, sooner if no improvement.

Quality checks:

● Missing / expected elements:
  – No vital signs recorded (BP, pulse, temperature).  
  – Exact ibuprofen dose (mg) not documented.  
  – Past surgical history, immunizations, menstrual/contraceptive history not explored.  

● Transcript vs DDx conflicts: None noted.

● Transcript quality: Clear history but limited physical exam and no vitals due to tele-consult; otherwise coherent.
